chapter: Changing styles, the road and nightlife
title: What killed Chicago nightlife: Daley's licences and crime
summary: Closing-hour licences and fear of crime emptied the clubs.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: What killed all that, do you think?

Well, one of the main things was when Mayor Daley come in. He shut down the licenses on night clubs. They were hard on them, and very few of them had the four o'clock licenses, and they cost more. And a lot of them had to close at 2:00, the 2:00 licenses. And that was one of the things that caused -- and then, I don't know, crime and all of that started seeping in, and all those people stopped
going out. They were afraid. And all the big cities started suffering the same thing.

Times changed, right. Muggings, and people didn't feel safe, so the respectable people just wouldn't go. And they're still that way. Now they're very choosy as to where they go, because they inquire if they're going to be safe.
